messages:
maya: Morning — following up on ticket INC-4821. Customer reports objects with TTL=30d remain visible after TTL expired. Do we have repro steps? @arjun any infra insight?
AcmeCorp-SRE: We noticed 3 object IDs still searchable even though TTL expired. Example IDs: obj_aa12, obj_bb34, obj_cc56. delete_request shows in audit.
maya: Thanks — can you paste the search query + audit log entries you see?
AcmeCorp-SRE: search: GET /v1/objects?q=obj_aa12 -> returns object meta + content. auditlog: "delete_request" for obj_aa12 at 2025-11-01T12:02:03Z, status=queued
arjun: From infra: queued typically means queued to deletion worker. We saw a spike in tombstone processing last hour. Can you give deletion-queue status? @deletion-bot can you show queue_len for tenant acmecorp?
delection-bot: (typo check)
meant: deletion-bot: tenant=acmecorp queue_len=0, last_processed=2025-11-01T12:05:10Z, last_error=nil
liam: Security note: KMS reported an intermittent HSM "lockout" window 2025-11-01T11:58-12:06 UTC in region-us-west-2. If KMS couldn't unwrap DEK, deletes would be deferred. Check auditlog for kms_unwrap_fail events.
AcmeCorp-SRE: Audit snippet: kms_unwrap_fail for obj_bb34 at 2025-11-01T12:01:57Z, reason="hsm-temporary-unavailable"
maya: That aligns. We have a 24h grace window for deletions when KMS issues happen so we don't accidentally destroy data during key outages. But TTL should still mark them scheduled. Why still searchable after grace?
arjun: Two possibilities: (1) grace window still active if we didn't complete unwrapping; (2) index cleanup job failed to remove entry from search index. Checking indexer logs now.
arjun: indexer log: 11/01 12:06:10 ERROR indexer/shard-7: failed delete for obj_aa12, reason=KV-store-timeout; retrying
AcmeCorp-SRE: For compliance they need explicit proof deletion occurred and timeline.
liam: Treat as P1 compliance. @maya open compliance incident and notify legal. Collect proof of deletion when done (delete_complete + index_remove events).
maya: Opening incident INC-4821-COMP now. In the meantime, workaround: admin-triggered delete exists but it still requires KMS unwrap; if HSM down manual KMS failover is required.
arjun: quick repro we used internally:
```
# check object
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood/run/v1/objects/obj_aa12
# internal force-delete (requires ops perms)
POST /internal/admin/delete { "object_id": "obj_aa12" }
```
maya: ETA: infra will clear backlog + reindex within ~2-4 hours if HSM recovers. If HSM keeps failing, ops must fail over to standby HSM (manual).
AcmeCorp-SRE: Ok — please confirm once deleted and attach audit proof. Also confirm retention policy remains 30d, not extended.
liam: Confirmed retention policy unchanged (30d). We'll attach KMS incident summary and audit entries once done.
arjun: updating thread when indexer retries succeed.
delection-bot: again typo, ignore
delection-bot: audit: delete_complete obj_aa12 at 2025-11-01T12:18:40Z; index_remove queued
arjun: indexer: index_remove completed for obj_aa12 at 2025-11-01T12:19:05Z :white_check_mark:
AcmeCorp-SRE: Verified via GET now returns 404. Thanks — please publish timeline for legal.
maya: Closing loop: objects removed after HSM recovered and indexer retries. Compliance incident INC-4821-COMP created and exported (timeline + audit) to AcmeCorp. Marking resolved; reopen if anything else.
